ruling.recommended_action: Escalate the 21:58–22:05 off-route segment to a human reviewer: confirm whether the car actually drove Tampines Avenue 7; if it did not, issue a voucher refund of $3.00 (2.13 km × $1.4098/km) under RD-2; do not attach any account action (RD-6 not met).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip was a metered RydeTAXI run, so distance feeds the fare: actual 20.1 km against 17.5 km optimal, +2.6 km, and the fare record shows distance $28.28 over 20.06 km plus a billed excess of 2.58 km at $1.4098/km [F1][F4][F7]. Under RD-2 the recoverable sum is only the unexempted off-route segment's extra_km × this trip's per-km rate, so the rider cannot recover the whole $42.25 [F4][F7][RD-2].

One off-route segment is recorded, 21:58–22:05, 4.04 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.90 km, +2.13 km and up to 1209 m off the optimal line [F3]. It is therefore a segment under review for RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5, and no percentage threshold applies [F3][RD-1].

Traffic does not exempt it: no incident was recorded near the route [F15], so RD-4(a) is unavailable, and the only congestion item is Tampines Expressway at speed band 2 during 21:33–21:58 [F12], which under RD-4(b) is corroboration only and cannot exempt a segment on its own [F12][F15][RD-4].

The decisive question is the scope of the rider's consent. The driver proposed a specific named road at 21:55 ("can I go round via Tampines Avenue 7?") and the rider answered at 21:56 "可以，走 Tampines Avenue 7 吧" — that is a designated-road authorisation, and it was sent before the segment started at 21:58, so RD-5's timing limb is met [F8][F9][F3][RD-5]. But such consent covers driving on that road only, and the record must tie the driven segment to it. Nothing does: no road name appears in any fact about the driven path, no stop or locating message places the car on Tampines Avenue 7, and the driver's own post-trip statement is not consent and cannot supply the missing link [F8][F9][F11][F3][RD-5]. Because the fact table carries no road names for the driven path, the correspondence between the agreed road and the actual segment cannot be settled from the record, so the finding is undetermined, and since it changes the amount the case goes to a person [F3][F8][F9][F11][RD-5].

RD-3 does not apply: no rider message named a place and no stop is measured in the segment, so there is nothing to exempt on that branch [F8][F9][F3][RD-3]. RD-6 is not met — 0 route disputes upheld in 90 days — so no account flag attaches, and the driver's other upheld disputes and the rider's clean profile are not used to decide this case [F18][RD-6].

If the segment were left unexempted the arithmetic would be 2.13 km × $1.4098/km = $3.00 ($28.28 ÷ 20.06 km = $1.4098/km) [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]; the $0.11 waiting item is metered waiting time kept by the driver on a RydeTAXI trip and is not refundable [F5][RD-3]. Since the segment's status is undetermined and it changes the amount, the ruling is escalate rather than a partial refund.

Safety screen: the chat is two complete, timestamped messages and the driver's statement is a plain factual account; I read them and found no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so safety_concern is none [F8][F9][F10][F11][SAFE-1].

D2 itself concedes the consent is narrow: naming Tampines Avenue 7 [F8][F9] confines the authorisation to driving on that road, and with no record tying the segment [F3] to that road the designation does not exempt the segment under RD-5 [F3][F9][RD-5].

A complete, timestamped chat record [F10] settles when messages were sent, not where the car went; the two messages contain no fact placing the segment on Tampines Avenue 7, so completeness does not satisfy RD-5's scope limb [F10][F3][F8][F9][RD-5].

Band 2 on Tampines Expressway [F12] is corroboration only under RD-4(b) and cannot exempt a segment on its own, and RD-4(a) is unavailable since no incident was recorded [F15], so this evidence does not exempt the segment [F12][F15][RD-4].

Accepted as far as it goes: RD-2 does cap any refund at the segment's extra_km × $1.4098/km, but the cap is not a bar to refunding the unexempted segment, whose status is undetermined [F3][F4][F7][RD-2].

Accepted: metered waiting time on a RydeTAXI trip is kept by the driver under RD-3(c), so the $0.11 item is not refunded, but this does not dispose of the distance excess in the off-route segment [F5][F3][RD-3].
Accepted: with 0 route disputes upheld in 90 days [F18], RD-6's predicate fails and no flag_account is attached; profile facts decide nothing else [F17][F18][RD-6].

C4's conclusion that the road-to-segment match is undetermined is adopted, but the consequence under RD-5/G13 for a segment whose status changes the amount is escalation to a human, not the partial refund C4 requests [F3][F8][F9][F11][RD-5].
Accepted: band 2 on Tampines Expressway [F12] is corroboration only under RD-4(b) and no incident was recorded [F15], so the congestion record does not exempt the segment [F12][F15][RD-4].

The formula 2.13 km × $1.4098/km = $3.00 [F3][F4] is correct arithmetic and the $0.11 waiting item is non-refundable [F5][RD-3], but the amount cannot be awarded while the segment's status is undetermined, so this claim cannot be executed [F3][RD-2][RD-5].
